title: Incorporating Worked Examples Into the Onboarding Process
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article borrows the education concept of 'Worked Examples' and applies it to employee onboarding. Rather than throwing new hires straight into unfamiliar real-world scenarios, a Worked Example shows them a problem that has already been expertly solved, including the origin of the problem, the step-by-step process used, and the resulting high-quality solution. The author cites research showing this approach helps newcomers learn faster than being asked to solve equivalent problems from scratch. The technique can be built around almost any procedural task, from sales pitches to negotiations to decision analysis, and is especially valuable when someone is learning a completely new skill. The piece frames onboarding speed as the real measure of program quality, with Worked Examples positioned as one of the fastest levers available.
points: Worked Examples show new hires an already-solved problem, not just a scenario to solve themselves
A good Worked Example includes the problem's origin, the step-by-step process, and the final solution
Research indicates Worked Examples accelerate learning compared to unguided problem-solving
The technique applies broadly, from sales strategy to presentations to negotiation
Onboarding quality should be measured by how quickly new hires become able to contribute
quotes: The sooner the new team member is ready to make an impact, the better the onboarding process.
Best-of-class onboarding processes include a heavy dose of what in education circles are called “Worked Examples.
A Worked Example provides learners with the origin of a problem or challenge, the procedure or step-by-step process used for solving the problem, and the high-quality solution.
Research has shown those new to a workplace who receive lots of Worked Examples learn new content and approaches more effectively than those who are asked to solve the same problem for themselves.
They are particularly powerful when learning something brand new or during the acquisition of unproven skills or competencies.
Onboarding is all about getting people ready for action. Worked Examples get that done.
